name: betelgeuse
label: Betelgeuse (alpha Ori, M1-2 Ia-ab)
sources: Montarges et al. 2014, A&A 572, A17 (VLTI/AMBER H and K): limb-darkened diameter 42.28 mas (uniform disk 41.01); Ohnaka et al. 2011: 42.49 +/- 0.06 mas
Joyce et al. 2020, ApJ 902, 63: parallax 5.95 (+0.58/-0.85) mas -> 168 (+27/-15) pc; Harper et al. 2017 (ALMA + e-MERLIN) 222 (+34/-48) pc
Ducati 2002 (yCat II/237): V 0.42, H -3.73, K -4.05; SIMBAD coordinates
Borisov et al. 2023: T_eff 3779 +/- 38 K (literature 3250-3690); mass 14 Msun (Neuhauser 2022; 9.5-21 in modern models)
notes: Semi-regular variable, V 0.0-1.6: the anchors are mean values.
First null 1.22 lambda/theta: 9.3 m at 1550 nm, 5.4 m at 900 nm -- the ISI's whole |V|^2 structure sits within 3-40 m.
The near-IR diameter is the photosphere; at 900 nm the TiO bands and the molecular layers make the star look larger (ISI's own 11 um result: 55 mas).
Anchors are Vega magnitudes converted with the band table's Vega -> AB offsets (V +0.02, H +1.39, K +1.85); 900 and 1550 nm fall inside the anchored range.
The radius is derived from theta_LD and the distance. No NewEra model exists below 4700 K: blackbody + linear law.
